answer_1.quote: Recent advances in techniques for generating realistic synthetic content (i.e., deepfakes) pose a diverse set of problems with significant societal consequences. The advent of large language models for text generation have made it easier than ever to create convincing synthetic text.
answer_1.outputs: The paper focuses on detecting machine-generated technical text, particularly generated or tampered scientific abstracts and full-length research papers. The generated outputs are synthetic paragraphs and abstracts created using GPT-2 domain-tuned on technical text, and the detection outputs are binary classifications (real vs. generated) and document-level tampering scores.

answer_2.quote: Detection performance on Semantic Scholar abstracts depends on the model used for task-tuning (RoBERTa-base, RoBERTa-large, or RoBERTa-large-STEM), the proxy domain (biomedical, physics, or biomedical-physics), and the number of proxy and SME samples used for task-tuning...

answer_4.quote: We assume the defender has access to a small number of examples from the adversary, which can be labeled by a subject matter expert (SME) as real (human) or synthetic (generated).
answer_4.guideline: Subject matter experts (SMEs) label abstracts or paragraphs as real (human-written) or synthetic (generated). The evaluation is binary classification based on authenticity.
